unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking to qualify as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three criteria are required: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding leave commencement, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In meeting the requirement that an employee must have been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when there is a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Must be counted where either (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee's break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee has an absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement than would be available under USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, or when determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years in determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in this section prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, but if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act for determining compensable hours of work, based on the number of hours worked within the meaning of the FLSA rather than methods of recordkeeping or non-reflective compensation agreements.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the requisite 1,250 hours.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, which are added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining the hours that would have been worked during a period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations in order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.modality_quote: must be able to clearly demonstrate
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In ascertaining an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits regarding whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles of the worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave, and once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility for that specific notice is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles, whether leave is taken all at once or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee leave has already started and the worksite employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed, but the employer expects the count to drop below 50 before leave commences.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave at a time when the 50-employee threshold within 75 miles is met, even if the employer expects the number of employees to drop below 50 by the time the period of leave begins.
